solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags.note: Can be solved by plugging in f(x)=0 (g=12, h=4), bypassing transformation reasoning; acceptable for SAT.

Q064-01.notes: g(x)=3(f(x)+4)=3f(x)+12; h(x)=3f(x)+4; difference 8. Likely trap answer 0 (thinking order doesn't matter).

flags.note: Answer key should accept 62.25 and 249/4 (both fit SPR grid). Trap answer 61 (the given equal heights) is likely.
Desmos regression on the 3 points gives the vertex directly.

Q064-02.notes: Symmetry: h(3)=h(4) so vertex at t=3.5. Second difference -10 so a=-5. h(t)=-5(t-3.5)^2+k, h(3)=61 gives k=62.25. Check h(2)=-5(2.25)+62.25=51.

Q064-03.notes: Two-year factor 32805/40500=0.81, annual factor 0.9; purchase value 40500/0.81=50000. A 45000=40500/0.9 (one year back only). B 48195=40500+7695 (linear extrapolation of the two-year drop). C 49005=40500*1.21 (inverting by multiplying by 1.1 twice).

flags.note: Can verify numerically: N(6)/N(0)=2 with a calculator, or check each option.

Q064-04.notes: 2^(t/4)*2^(-t/12)=2^(t/6), doubles every 6 hours. A ignores the decay factor; C uses 12-4=8; D uses 4+12=16.

flags.note: Test-value check: plugging each option into 2x-1 and seeing which gives 3 identifies B quickly; inherent to the skill.

Q064-05.notes: q(x)=0 when 2x-1=3, i.e., x=2. A: 2(1)-1=1, not 3. C: copies the zero of p (2*3-1=5). D: maps 3 forward via 2x-1 instead of solving.

flags.note: Test function f(x)=(x-4)^2 eliminates all distractors immediately; standard for this item type.

Q064-06.notes: Axis x=4, opens up; values increase with distance from 4. A: dist 4 vs 1, true. B: dist 3 vs 3, equal, false. C: f(4) is the minimum, false. D: dist 1 vs 4, reversed, false.

flags.note: Trap 60 (linear extrapolation of +20 per 3 weeks) is likely.
Desmos with a slider for a shows 3 intersections for any a>0, bypassing the algebra.

Q064-08.notes: Let u=x-2: |u|=a u^2 gives u=0 or |u|=1/a, so x=2, 2+1/a, 2-1/a: three points. A counts only the vertex; B misses the shared vertex point; D overcounts.

Q064-09.notes: a+b=6 (vertex x is the average of the zeros); f(3)=9-3(a+b)+ab=-9+ab=-4 so ab=5 (zeros 1 and 5).

flags.note: Desmos: graphing y=sqrt(x+k) and y=x for each listed k resolves it without the algebra.

Q064-10.notes: Need x>=0 and x^2-x-k=0 with two nonnegative roots: 1+4k>0 and -k>=0, so -1/4<k<=0. k=-0.2: roots ~0.276, 0.724, both valid. A k=-0.3: discriminant negative, no solutions. C k=0.2: roots of opposite sign, only one valid. D k=2: x=2 only (x=-1 extraneous).

flags.note: Partial-credit cue: A is the discriminant-only answer, so the student who knows about the excluded value x=2 sees D as the extension of A.

Q064-12.notes: x^2-2x-k=0 with x!=2. k=-1: double root x=1, valid. k=0: roots 0 and 2; x=2 excluded, leaving x=0 only. Otherwise discriminant>0 and neither root is 2, so two solutions; or no solution if k<-1. A misses k=0. B: k=1 gives 1+/-sqrt2, two solutions. C includes 1 (wrong) and leaves out -1.
